serverworks.manual.building.body:
A rack is a hollow box of Rack Casing, 3 to 7 blocks along each side. Edges and corners must be casing; components go on the faces; the inside stays empty.
The weakest casing sets the limits: iron racks allow 4 GB and 10 players, diamond 8 GB and 40, netherite 16 GB and 100. Use a Rack Wrench on any rack block to outline everything still missing.
serverworks.manual.building.title: Building a Rack
serverworks.manual.disks.body:
Craft Blank Disks, then put one in a Disk Writer. Search the catalog, click a project or drag it onto the right-hand panel, and take the written disk from the output slot. It carries the project's name and icon.
Write a modpack and you get a Pack Cartridge instead. Disks only name a project: the newest version that suits your rack is chosen when the server starts.
serverworks.manual.disks.title: Disks and the Disk Writer
serverworks.manual.heading: Operator's Manual
serverworks.manual.joining.body:
Use the Gateway while the server runs: your world is saved and you arrive on the rack's server. Press B there (change it in Controls), or press Escape and choose Return, to go back.
If a disk needs to be installed by players too, the Gateway stays amber and names it. Save the Client Pack from the Server Core and import it into the Modrinth App or Prism Launcher.
serverworks.manual.joining.title: Joining Your Server
serverworks.manual.limits.body:
A server with nobody on it for ten minutes goes to sleep. Using its Gateway wakes it up.
Up to six rack servers can run at once on one computer. Each keeps its world in the serverworks folder of your game directory, so stopping a rack never loses anything.
serverworks.manual.limits.title: Sleep and Limits
serverworks.manual.modpacks.body:
A rack can hold one Pack Cartridge alongside its disks. The modpack must be for this Minecraft version and the rack's platform.
Its server-side mods and settings are installed when the server starts. Players need the whole pack, which the Client Pack button saves for you.
serverworks.manual.modpacks.title: Pack Cartridges
serverworks.manual.parts.body:
Server Core: the controls. One per rack.
Platform Module: picks the server software. One per rack.
Drive Bay: holds eight disks. Memory Bank: 1 GB each, on top of 1 GB to start.
Vent: one for every four Drive Bays and Memory Banks.
Gateway and Status Display are optional: the way in, and a screen showing who is on.
serverworks.manual.parts.title: Rack Components
serverworks.manual.platforms.body:
Vanilla runs data packs. Fabric, Quilt, NeoForge and Forge run mods. Paper, Purpur, Folia, Spigot, CraftBukkit and Sponge run plugins. Velocity and BungeeCord are proxies that join several racks into one network.
Disks that cannot run on the rack's platform are tinted red in the Server Core. Spigot and CraftBukkit are compiled the first time they are used, which takes several minutes.
serverworks.manual.platforms.title: Platforms
serverworks.manual.proxies.body:
Sneak-use a Link Card on a rack's Server Core to point it at that rack. Put Link Cards in a Velocity or BungeeCord rack's Drive Bay.
Starting the proxy starts every linked rack, reachable only through the proxy. Players arrive on the first linked rack and can move between them with the proxy's /server command.
serverworks.manual.proxies.title: Proxies and Link Cards
serverworks.manual.recipes.disks: Mod Disks and Pack Cartridges are not crafted: write them in the Disk Writer from a Blank Disk.
serverworks.manual.recipes.title: Recipes
serverworks.manual.starting.body:
Open the Server Core and press Start. The first time, you will be asked to agree to the Minecraft EULA for this computer.
The core shows downloads, then the address to join. The Console tab shows the server's output and takes commands. In singleplayer only you can start racks; on a server, only operators can.
serverworks.manual.starting.title: Starting a Server
serverworks.manual.subheading: Everything about building and running racks
serverworks.manual.trouble.body:
Rack not forming? Use the Rack Wrench: blue outlines need a block, orange ones are in the wrong place, red ones must be cleared from inside.
Server failed? The Console tab shows why. Hovering over the error in the Server Core shows the details. A disk with no version for your platform or Minecraft version is the usual cause.
serverworks.manual.trouble.title: Troubleshooting
serverworks.manual.welcome.body:
Serverworks turns Minecraft servers into machines you build. A server rack holds the software, the mods and plugins you load into it, and a Gateway you can walk through to play on it.
Every rack runs a real server on this computer, downloaded from the official sources and from Modrinth, the catalog all the disks come from.
